ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a regular nonagon, and on the right side there are two lines extended from the boundary of the nonagon that intersect at point X, forming a sharp angle. The upper extended line is drawn out from the vertex at the upper right of the nonagon, and the lower extended line is drawn out from the vertex at the lower right of the nonagon; between these two contact vertices there also passes through one right-side vertex of the nonagon. Then reason: Mark the upper contact point as A, the middle right-side vertex as B, and the lower contact point as C. Each exterior angle of a regular nonagon is 360°/9 = 40°. To turn from the direction of the upper extended side to the direction of the lower extended side, it is necessary to pass through three consecutive turns of side direction, so the total turn angle is 3 × 40° = 120°. The angle marked at point X is the smaller supplementary angle formed by these two extended lines, therefore X = 180° - 120° = 60°.

method.method_draft: Label the two nonagon vertices where the sides to X touch as A, the intervening rightmost vertex as B, and the lower touch vertex as C. From the image, the upper segment AX is the continuation of the nonagon side just before A, and the lower segment CX is the continuation of the nonagon side just after C. From the text, the polygon is a regular nonagon, so each exterior turn is 360/9 = 40 degrees. Moving along the regular nonagon from the upper extended side to the lower extended side involves three successive side-direction turns, totaling 3 × 40 = 120 degrees. The angle between the two extended lines at X is the smaller supplementary angle, 180 - 120 = 60 degrees.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a concave quadrilateral A-X-C-B, where A is the upper contact vertex, C is the lower contact vertex, and B is the rightmost nonagon vertex between them. The sides AX and CX are extensions of adjacent nonagon sides outside the polygon. Since the nonagon is regular, each interior angle is (9 - 2)180/9 = 140 degrees, so each exterior angle is 40 degrees. Therefore the quadrilateral angles at A and C are each 40 degrees, because they are formed by an extended side and the next nonagon side. At B, the quadrilateral uses the reflex angle outside the nonagon, equal to 360 - 140 = 220 degrees. The angles of quadrilateral A-X-C-B sum to 360 degrees, so X = 360 - 40 - 40 - 220 = 60 degrees.
